jobs.prompt:
ci(cpp): compiler cache for the native gateway's builds (driver, CI workflows, documentation)

CONTEXT (you have no other context than this prompt and the repository)
You start from branch `agent-jobs/cppgw-cpp-only-20261119-44610457899-1` of ubiquity/ai.ubq.fi: the native C++20 gateway (`cpp/gateway/`), C++ only (do NOT install or run Bun, Node, Deno, Rust or Cargo). Its builds are slow because everything is compiled from scratch every time: the hosted CI (`.github/workflows/cpp-gateway-ci.yml`, runner `ubuntu-26.04-arm`) runs four release shards, four sanitizer shards and about twenty fuzz jobs, and EACH job compiles all ~370 production objects and the vendored libraries again; coding agents on fresh runners do the same. The portable driver is `bash cpp/gateway/tools/ci-build.sh --config release|asan [--shard N/4 | <test>]` (read `cpp/gateway/docs/CI.md`, `cpp/gateway/cmake/ci/*.py` and `cpp/gateway/fuzz/ci.py` to see how compile commands are formed and where objects go). Your branch becomes a pull request; your final message is its body: short, plain language, with measured before/after times.

YOUR MACHINE: GitHub-hosted Linux ARM64 runner, Ubuntu 26.04, 4 CPUs, 16 GB, sudo, network. `sudo apt-get install -y clang ninja-build pkg-config ccache libboost-json-dev libboost-container-dev libssl-dev libsqlite3-dev zlib1g-dev libicu-dev libbrotli-dev libzstd-dev` gives a toolchain that builds this tree (the CI workflow shows the exact package list and how it builds the pinned SQLite: do the same). The environment has `CCACHE_DIR` set to a directory that is restored before and saved after your job; `ccache` is installed.

RULES
- The runner holds a model gateway token: never print it or write any credential to a file. Run tests with an empty `HOME`, a fresh `TMPDIR` and no provider variables; local mocks only.
- Your process can be restarted without warning and then knows only what is committed: commit after each step, keep a checklist in `cpp/gateway/docs/findings/cppgw-build-cache-20261119.md`, read it and `git log` first after a restart. No foreground command longer than about 10 minutes: run long builds in the background and poll.
- Do not delete or weaken tests. Do not change what is compiled or with which flags: only how compile results are reused.

TASK
1. Driver: make every compile the driver, the fuzz builder and the packagers launch go through a compiler launcher when one is available: honour `UOS_CI_COMPILER_LAUNCHER` (explicit; empty string disables) and otherwise use `ccache` if it is on PATH. The cache must be CORRECT: results keyed on compiler binary content, full command line, preprocessed input and the config (release/asan/fuzz); set `CCACHE_BASEDIR` to the repository root and `CCACHE_NOHASHDIR`/`-fdebug-prefix-map` handling so two checkouts in different directories share hits; `CCACHE_COMPILERCHECK=content`; make sure `-MD`/dependency files, sanitizer flags, coverage/fuzz instrumentation and the precomputed input digests the driver records still work. The driver's receipts must say whether a launcher was used and print `ccache --show-stats` deltas (hits, misses) at the end.
2. Stop compiling the same production objects once per job where the driver can share them: check whether the driver already compiles each production source once per config per invocation (it reports "objects reused"); if separate CI jobs of the same config rebuild identical objects, that is exactly what the cache fixes: do not restructure the matrix.
3. CI workflows (`cpp-gateway-ci.yml`, `cpp-gateway-release.yml` Linux job): install `ccache`, add `actions/cache` (pinned to commit `0057852bfaa89a56745cba8c7296529d2fc39830`, v4, using its `restore` and `save` sub-actions) for `CCACHE_DIR` with a key of the form `ccache-<runner image>-<config>-<hash of the toolchain package versions and vendored sources>-<run id>` and a `restore-keys` prefix without the run id; one cache per config (release, asan, fuzz) shared by that config's shards, saved only from ONE designated job per config (e.g. shard 1) to avoid ten concurrent saves; cap each with `CCACHE_MAXSIZE` so the three together stay under 6 GB (GitHub's limit is 10 GB per repository). The release-package workflow must NOT restore a cache for the artefact it publishes (a release build compiles clean); say so in a comment. Validate with `actionlint` (Go binary; installing it is fine).
4. Measure on your runner and record: cold release shard 1 (empty cache) wall time and object-phase time; the same shard again after `git clean` of all build output with the warm cache; the same from a second checkout in a different directory; one sanitizer shard cold and warm. State hit rates. Then correctness: change one header that many sources include, rebuild, and show that exactly the dependent objects miss; revert it.
5. `cpp/gateway/docs/CI.md`: a short section on the cache (how to use it locally, how to disable it, how CI keys it).

DONE WHEN
Warm rebuilds of an unchanged tree hit the cache for at least 95% of compiles in release and sanitizer configs, the header-change check shows correct invalidation, the workflows pass `actionlint`, and the report has the measured times.
